data.reason: Modem has been back to OPERATIONAL/registered since 02:28-02:29 (modem-events.jsonl, modem-metrics.jsonl), but gw.lan's vtnet0 still carries the pre-reboot lease (198.51.100.27 from dhcp-server-identifier 203.0.113.67) and cannot reach the ISP side (ping 198.51.100.1: 100% loss). The watchdog logged "would_reload" at 02:30 and again at 02:40 because it is in observe mode, so no reload ever happened. Reconfiguring the WAN interface to renew its DHCP lease is the pending step needed to restore internet.

data.error: action must be one of: change_config, contact_provider, investigate_further, none, reboot_host, replace_hardware, restart_service
host must be one of: gw.lan, mon.lan, external

data.component: WAN interface vtnet0 / ISP DHCP lease (stale after upstream loss and modem reboot); watchdog in observe mode never applied a reload
data.cause: The provider link dropped at 02:01:44 when the cable modem lost upstream sync (T3 time-out) and later rebooted and re-registered, but gw.lan's WAN interface was never reconfigured afterwards — the watchdog only logs "would_reload" in observe mode — so the firewall kept using a stale ISP lease and could not reach the provider side even after the modem reported OPERATIONAL at 02:28-02:29.
evidence: ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1 (gw.lan) -> 3 packets transmitted, 0 received, 100% packet loss: the ISP-side gateway is unreachable although the default route via 198.51.100.1 on vtnet0 is present (netstat -rn).
ifconfig vtnet0 -> UP,BROADCAST,RUNNING,SIMPLEX,MULTICAST,LOWER_UP, inet 198.51.100.27, status active: layer 2 toward the provider CPE is up, so the failure is above the physical link.

cat /var/db/dhclient.leases.vtnet0 -> still holds fixed-address 198.51.100.27 with dhcp-server-identifier 203.0.113.67 and renew time 2026/3/5; the lease predates the outage and was never renewed after the modem re-registered.

/var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl -> 02:01:44 'No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out' (outage start), 02:14:10 'TFTP failed - configuration file NOT FOUND', 02:28:21 'Cable Modem Reboot ... registration complete'.

/var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-metrics.jsonl -> status NOT_SYNCHRONIZED at 02:06, then OPERATIONAL at 02:29 and 02:40 (modem uptime 1620s then 2280s): the modem had already recovered ~12 minutes before the reported time.

/var/db/wan-watchdog/events.jsonl -> decision 'none' (modem_not_operational) at 02:06, 'none' (modem_settling) at 02:29, then action 'reload' / event 'would_reload' at 02:30 and again 'would_reload' (retry) at 02:40, mode observe: no reload was ever applied.
cat /var/db/wan-watchdog/state.json -> {"reloads_in_outage": 2, "last_action": "reload", "modem_op_since": 1772522940} while the outage is still ongoing at 02:41.
ping -c 3 -n 10.20.0.1 from mon.lan -> 0% packet loss: LAN/local services are healthy, isolating the fault to the WAN path.
data.recommendation: Reconfigure/restart gw.lan's WAN interface (vtnet0) so it drops the stale lease and renews its address from the provider — this is the pending wan_reload that the observe-mode watchdog identified but never performed; internet should return once a fresh lease is installed. Longer term, switch the watchdog from observe mode to an enforcing mode so a recovered modem actually triggers a WAN renew, and have the ISP check the upstream line / modem config-file fetch if T3 time-outs recur.
